prompt: Document our food delivery order lifecycle as sequence diagram(s) for the engineering wiki (GitHub renders mermaid). The flow: the customer places an order in the mobile app; the app calls the API gateway, which forwards to the Order Service (POST /orders); the Order Service persists the order as PENDING in its Postgres, then calls the Payment Service (POST /payments), which authorizes the card with Stripe and replies approved or declined; if declined, the Order Service marks the order FAILED and the app shows the error. If approved, the Order Service publishes order.paid to Kafka; the Restaurant Service consumes it and pushes the order to the restaurant's tablet, and the restaurant accepts or rejects — reject means refund via the Payment Service, order CANCELLED, customer notified. When accepted, the Restaurant Service publishes order.accepted; the Courier Service consumes it, finds the nearest available courier, offers the job (a courier can decline, in which case it retries with the next courier), and assigns it; the courier picks up and delivers, marking PICKED_UP and DELIVERED through the Courier Service, which publishes status events. The Notification Service consumes all order.* events and sends a push notification to the customer at each stage (paid, accepted, courier assigned, picked up, delivered). Show the whole thing including the failure branches I mentioned.
assertions: The output is split into two or more fenced mermaid blocks (by phase or scenario), not one giant diagram
Every mermaid block parses successfully with mermaid-cli (exit 0)
No single diagram exceeds roughly 25 messages
Participant names/labels are consistent across the diagrams (the same service uses the same label everywhere)
Each diagram has its own heading and short introduction, and continuity between diagrams is made explicit
All described failure branches appear: payment declined -> order FAILED, restaurant reject -> refund + CANCELLED + customer notified, courier decline -> retry with next courier
Only widely-supported (safe-core) mermaid syntax is used, since GitHub rendering was requested
